incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert - SEV2 - ModelConfigMismatch - PD-4729 triggered for #incidents. Summary: catalog promotion caused default revision for model 'text-highthroughput' to change to 'rev-2026-03-14-test' which uses tokenizer 'sentencepiece-v2' while runtime expects 'bpe-v1'. Spike in 5xxs and garbled tokens observed. https://pagerduty.example/PD-4729

pagerduty: Alert routed to @maya, @leo, escalation policy: infra-oncall -> eng-sre.

maya: acked. I'm on call, investigating now. pulling recent logs and metrics.

sam: seeing big jump on /generate/text-highthroughput: error_rate 0.3% -> 8% over last 10m, latency up ~20%. Logs contain tokenizer mismatch errors. sample log:
```
2026-03-14T15:12:03Z ERROR tokenizer.cpp:58 InvalidTokenizer: expected bpe-v1 but got sentencepiece-v2 (model=text-highthroughput, rev=rev-2026-03-14-test, request_id=abc123)
2026-03-14T15:12:04Z WARN serving.cpp:102 fallback encoded tokens look garbled for tenant=tenant-acme
```

anika: confirmed - the catalog import pipeline accidentally promoted a test revision that had an experimental tokenizer override used for local eval. The pipeline's promotion rule allowed it through because the model metadata schema check missed tokenizer field.

leo: recommendation: immediate mitigation steps - 1) pin route to last known good revision rev-2026-03-01 2) apply temporary rate-limit to the route 3) rollback catalog default if necessary. This should stop the garbled outputs quickly.

maya: running rollback/pin now.

maya: ```bash
# pin the route to previous good revision
redwoodctl route update --route text-highthroughput --pin-revision rev-2026-03-01 --reason "emergency pin due to tokenizer mismatch PD-4729"
# also set catalog default back as a safeguard
redwoodctl catalog set-default --model text-highthroughput --revision rev-2026-03-01
```

ops-bot: Command accepted. Executing: redwoodctl route update --route text-highthroughput --pin-revision rev-2026-03-01
ops-bot: Route update successful. Old default revision: rev-2026-03-14-test -> new default/pinned: rev-2026-03-01

sam: I've applied a temporary token-level throttle: 50 rps to the route and reduced canary percent to 0%.

ops-bot: Applied rate-limit. Canary traffic set to 0%.

pagerduty: PD-4729 acknowledged by maya. Escalation suppressed.

eng-monitoring-bot: Metrics update (5m window): error_rate on text-highthroughput fell from 8% -> 0.7%, latency trending back to normal. 12 tenants reported garbled outputs; one tenant reported ~2x latency.

maya: handoff: I'm handing the incident to @leo for watch and validation. I'll own the postmortem. Current status: routing pinned, rate-limited, catalog default reverted. Need follow-up: (a) prevent bad promotions (b) add tokenizer schema validation to catalog pipeline (c) add runbook step for emergency pin commands.

anika: filing PR to add tokenizer validation to the catalog promotion job and a unit test to cover tokenizer mismatches. Also reverting the test metadata in the staging catalog. PR: https://git.example/redwood/catalog/pull/829

leo: ack, I'll monitor for 30m and escalate if error_rate > 1% or if new 5xxs appear. I'll also coordinate with customer-success for the affected tenants.

maya: thanks team. creating incident ticket with timeline and assigning action items to owners. We'll keep PD open until stable for 30m.

leo: quick note for the runbook: add verification step: `redwoodctl catalog validate --check-tokenizer-match` before promotion.

maya: added to action list. :thumbsup: Good catch, everyone. I'll post the postmortem draft in #postmortems once done.

eng-monitoring-bot: Monitoring: last check 2026-03-14T15:30:00Z - error_rate 0.6% (down from peak). Continuing to poll every 60s.

maya: closing the Slack page for now but keeping PD open. If anything regresses ping me or @leo.

sam: noted. leaving traces for forensic logs and will collect sample requests for the affected tenants.

incident-bot: Incident PD-4729 still active (acknowledged). All mitigation steps recorded.

maya: end of thread for now.
